div.head: I Em 2
div.ab: Teoðunge we bebeodað ælcum Cristene men be his Cristendóme and ciricsceat ⁊ Romfeoh ⁊ sulhælmessan. And gif hit hwá don nelle, si he amansumod.
Teoðunge we bebeodaþ ælcum Cristenum men be his Cristendome ⁊ cyricsceat ⁊ ælmesfeoh. Gif hit hwa don nelle, sy he amansumod.
Teoðunge we bebeodað ælcum Cristenum men be his Cristendome ⁊ cyricsceat ⁊ ælmesfeoh. Gif hit hwa don nelle, sy he amansomod.
Decimam precipimus omni Christiano super Christianitatem suam et cyricsceatum (id est ecclesie censum) et ælmesfeoh (id est elemosine pecuniam). Si quis hoc dare nolit, excommunicatus sit.
[Be teoþungum ⁊ cyricsceatum.] Teoðunge we bebeodað ælcum Cristene men be his Cristendóme, and ciricsceat ⁊ Romfeoh ⁊ sulhælmessan. And gif hit hwa don nelle, si he amansumod.
Teoðunge we bebeodað ælcum Cristene men be his Cristendome and ciricsceat and Romfeoh and sulhælmessan. And gif hit hwa don nelle, si he amansumod.

(Von Zehnten und Kirchensteuern. Ld) Zehnt(en?) [an die Kirche zu zahlen] gebieten wir jedem Christenmenschen bei seinem Christenthume und Kirchensteuer und Romgeld [Peterspfennig] und Pflugalmosen. Und wenn das einer nicht thun will, sei er excommunicirt.

(Of tithes and church-dues. Ld) Tithe(s?) [to be paid to the church] we command of every Christian man by his Christianity, and church-scot and Rome-money [Peter's Pence] and plough-alms. And if anyone will not do it, let him be excommunicated.

We enjoin upon every Christian man, in accordance with his Christian profession, to pay tithes and church-dues and Peter's Pence and plough-alms. And if anyone refuses to do so, he shall be excommunicated.
We direct every Christian to pay tithes and Church dues and dues to Rome and plow dues in accordance with Christian doctrine. And if anyone refuses to do so, let him be excommunicated.
div.note: ‘Romfeoh ⁊ sulhælmessan’ only in D; H, B and Quadr. have ‘ælmesfeoh’ (alms-money). Liebermann compares EGu 6 f.

dues to Rome and plow dues: See notes to The Laws of Edward and Guthrum 6.1 and 6.3. These two forms of ecclesiastical dues are omitted from the versions of 1 Edmund preserved in Cambridge, Corpus Christi College MS 383, Textus Roffensis, and Quadripartitus. As with similar passages in 1 Æthelstan, it is likely these are an interpolation by Wulfstan.

Be teoþungum ⁊ cyricsceatum rubric in Ld

Singular verstehen Q und Thorpe, Plural Schmid. Letzterer müsste normal -a enden; doch wäre in Hss. 11./12. Jhs. -e dafür wohl möglich.—Vgl. Einl. 9; Gl Zehnt; Odos Hirtenbrief c. 10: Omnes studeant de omnibus quae possident dare decimas

Q and Thorpe understand a singular, Schmid a plural. The latter would normally end in -a; but in MSS of the 11th/12th cent. -e would probably be possible instead.—Cf. Introduction 9; Gl Zehnt; Odo's pastoral letter c. 10: Omnes studeant de omnibus quae possident dare decimas
Ebd. Peterspfennig 9. a. Wohl Zusatz D's; o. Einl. 8
Ibid. Peterspfennig 9. a. Probably an addition of D's; above Introduction 8
Ebd. Exkommunikation 11f. Weltliche Strafen drohen EGu 6 ff. VIII Atr 12
Ibid. Exkommunikation 11f. Secular penalties are threatened in EGu 6 ff. VIII Atr 12
Singular or plural? Q translates decimam.
Romfeoh ⁊ sulhælmæssan are mentioned only in D, whereas H, B and Q have simply ælmesfeoh. Is it possible that D has differentiated the payments which together make up ælmesfeoh?
